chapter.li: Verse36 And some days after, Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do. VerseEnd Verse37 And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. VerseEnd Verse38 But Paul thought not good to take with them him who departed from them from Pamphylia and went not with them to the work. VerseEnd Verse39 And the contention was so sharp between them that they departed asunder one from the other. And so Barnabas took Mark and sailed unto Cyprus, VerseEnd Verse40 and Paul chose Silas and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God. VerseEnd Verse41 And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches. VerseEnd

LEChapter16 Verse1 Then came he to Derbe and Lystra, and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy — the son of a certain woman who was a Jewess and believed, but his father was a Greek VerseEnd — Verse2 who was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium. VerseEnd Verse3 Him would Paul have to go forth with him, and took and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those quarters, for they knew all that his father was a Greek. VerseEnd Verse4 And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees to keep that were ordained of the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse5 And so were the churches established in the faith and increased in number daily. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia — and were forbidden of the holy ghost to preach the word in Asia VerseEnd — Verse7 after they had come to Mysia, they attempted to go into Bithynia, but the spirit suffered them not. VerseEnd Verse8 And they, passing by Mysia, came down to Troas. VerseEnd

Verse9 And a vision appeared to Paul in the night. There stood a man of Macedonia and implored him, saying, Come over into Macedonia and help us. VerseEnd Verse10 And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavored to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us to preach the gospel unto them. VerseEnd Verse11 Therefore, setting sail from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothrace, and the next day to Neapolis, VerseEnd Verse12 and from there to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia and a colony; and we were in that city staying certain days. VerseEnd

Verse13 And on the Sabbath, we went out of the city, by a riverside where the people gathered for prayer to be made. And we sat down and spoke unto the women who gathered there. VerseEnd Verse14 And a certain woman named Lydia — a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, who worshipped God — heard us, whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul. VerseEnd Verse15 And when she was baptized, and her household, she implored us, saying, If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and abide there. And she constrained us. VerseEnd

Verse16 And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by fortune-telling. VerseEnd Verse17 The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the Most High God, who show unto us the way of salvation! VerseEnd Verse18 And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour. VerseEnd

Verse19 And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers, VerseEnd Verse20 and brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city, VerseEnd Verse21 and teach customs which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans. VerseEnd Verse22 And the multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates rent off their clothes and commanded to beat them. VerseEnd Verse23 And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely VerseEnd — Verse24 who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks. VerseEnd

Verse25 And at midnight, Paul and Silas prayed and sang praises unto God, and the prisoners heard them. VerseEnd Verse26 And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s bands were loosened. VerseEnd Verse27 And the keeper of the prison, awaking out of his sleep and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had fled. VerseEnd Verse28 But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do yourself no harm, for we are all here! VerseEnd Verse29 Then he called for a light and sprang in, and came trembling and fell down before Paul and Silas, VerseEnd Verse30 and brought them out and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? VerseEnd Verse31 And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and you shall be saved, and your house. VerseEnd Verse32 And they spoke unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house. VerseEnd Verse33 And he took them the same hour of the night and washed their stripes and was baptized, he and all his, immediately. VerseEnd Verse34 And when he had brought them into his house, he set food before them and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house. VerseEnd

Verse35 And when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, Let those men go. VerseEnd Verse36 And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul: The magistrates have sent to let you go, now therefore depart and go in peace. VerseEnd Verse37 But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly, uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now they do thrust us out secretly? Nay, truly, but let them come themselves and fetch us out. VerseEnd Verse38 And the sergeants told these words unto the magistrates, and they feared when they heard that they were Romans. VerseEnd Verse39 And they came and implored them and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city. VerseEnd Verse40 And they went out of the prison and entered into the house of Lydia. And when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them and departed. VerseEnd

LEChapter17 Verse1 Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews. VerseEnd Verse2 And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three Sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures, VerseEnd Verse3 explaining and alleging that Christ needed to suffer and rise again from the dead, and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ. VerseEnd Verse4 And some of them believed and joined with Paul and Silas, and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few. VerseEnd

Verse5 But the Jews who believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd men of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city in an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people. VerseEnd Verse6 And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down have come here also, VerseEnd Verse7 whom Jason has received; and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king — one Jesus. VerseEnd Verse8 And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city when they heard these things. VerseEnd Verse9 And when they had taken security of Jason and of the other, they let them go. VerseEnd

Verse10 And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea, who, coming there, went into the synagogue of the Jews. VerseEnd Verse11 These were more noble than those in Thessalonica in that they received the word with all readiness of mind and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. VerseEnd Verse12 Therefore, many of them believed also of honorable women who were Greeks, and of men not a few. VerseEnd Verse13 But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came there also and stirred up the people. VerseEnd Verse14 And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as if it were to the sea, but Silas and Timothy remained there still, VerseEnd Verse15 and they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens. And receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timothy to come to him with all speed, they departed. VerseEnd

Verse16 Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout people, and in the market daily with them that met with him. VerseEnd Verse18 Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans and of the Stoics encountered him, and some said, What will this babbler say? Some others, He seems to be a proclaimer of strange gods — because he preached unto them Jesus and the resurrection. VerseEnd Verse19 And they took him and brought him unto the Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof you speak, is? VerseEnd Verse20 For you bring certain strange things to our ears. We would know therefore what these things mean. VerseEnd (Verse21 For all the Athenians and strangers who were there spent their time in nothing else but either to tell or to hear some new thing. VerseEnd)

Verse22 Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill and said, You men of Athens, I perceive that in all things you are too VerseEnd Verse23 superstitious; for as I passed by and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription: To the Unknown God. Whom therefore you ignorantly worship, him declare I unto VerseEnd Verse24 you. God, who made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwells not in temples made with VerseEnd Verse25 hands, neither is worshipped with men’s hands as though he needed anything, seeing he gives to all life, and breath, and all things; VerseEnd Verse26 and has made of one blood all nations of men to dwell on all the face of the earth; and has determined the times before appointed and the bounds of their habitation, VerseEnd Verse27 that they should seek the Lord if they are willing to find him. For he is not far from every one of us, VerseEnd Verse28 for in him we live, and move, and have our being. As certain also of your own poets have said: For we are also his offspring. VerseEnd Verse29 Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold or silver or stone, engraved by art and man’s device. VerseEnd Verse30 And the times of this ignorance, God overlooked, but now commands all men everywhere to repent, VerseEnd Verse31 because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by him whom he has ordained; and he has given assurance of this unto all men, in that he has raised him from the dead. VerseEnd

Verse32 And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked and others said, We will hear you again of this matter. VerseEnd Verse33 So Paul departed from among them. VerseEnd Verse34 Nevertheless, certain men cleaved unto him and believed, among whom were Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them. VerseEnd

LEChapter18 Verse1 After these things, Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth, VerseEnd Verse2 and found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla (because Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome), and came unto them. VerseEnd Verse3 And because he was of the same craft, he abided with them and worked — for by their occupation they were tentmakers. VerseEnd Verse4 And he reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks. VerseEnd

Verse5 And when Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ. VerseEnd Verse6 And when they opposed and blasphemed, he shook his raiment and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads, I am clean. From henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles. VerseEnd Verse7 And he departed from there and entered into a certain man’s house named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house was adjacent to the synagogue. VerseEnd Verse8 And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians, hearing, believed and were baptized. VerseEnd Verse9 Then spoke the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak and hold not your peace, VerseEnd Verse10 for I am with you and no man shall attack you to hurt you, for I have many people in this city. VerseEnd Verse11 And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them. VerseEnd

Verse12 And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul and brought him to the judgment seat, VerseEnd Verse13 saying, This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law. VerseEnd Verse14 And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O you Jews, reason would argue that I should bear with you. VerseEnd Verse15 But if it is a question of words and names and of your law, you look to it, for I will be no judge of such matters. VerseEnd Verse16 And he drove them from the judgment seat. VerseEnd Verse17 Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things. VerseEnd

Verse18 And Paul, after this, remained there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren and sailed from there into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila, having shorn his head in Cenchrea, for he had a vow. VerseEnd Verse19 And he came to Ephesus and left them there, but he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews. VerseEnd Verse20 When they desired him to remain longer time with them, he consented not, VerseEnd Verse21 but bid them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that comes in Jerusalem, but I will return again unto you if God desires. And he sailed from Ephesus. VerseEnd Verse22 And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch. VerseEnd Verse23 And after he had spent some time there, he departed and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples. VerseEnd
